quantum-communication.originalTitle: Multiplexing of Continuous-Variable and Discrete-Variable Quantum Key Distribution Systems over Fibered and Free-Space Channels
quantum-communication.catchyTitle: Multiplexing of Continuous-Variable and Discrete-Variable Quantum Key Distribution Systems over Fibered and Free-Space Channels
quantum-communication.headline: CV-QKD and DV-QKD can share one optical channel with no measurable penalty
quantum-communication.summary: CV-QKD suits short high-rate links and DV-QKD long lossy ones, but the two had never run together on one channel. Independent CV and DV systems were multiplexed with standard C-band DWDM filters over fiber and a 620 m daylight free-space link. On fiber both delivered about 1.43 Mbit/s at the 7.56 dB crossover, with no measurable added QBER or excess noise.

summaryParts.problem: CV-QKD suits short high-rate links and DV-QKD long lossy ones, but the two had never run together on one channel.

summaryParts.result: On fiber both delivered about 1.43 Mbit/s at the 7.56 dB crossover, with no measurable added QBER or excess noise.
summaryParts.limits: One fiber setup and one urban free-space link.

autism-diagnosis.originalTitle: Temporal Generalization in fNIRS-Based Autism Classification: A Cross-Time-Window Transfer Benchmark
autism-diagnosis.catchyTitle: Temporal Generalization in fNIRS-Based Autism Classification: A Cross-Time-Window Transfer Benchmark
autism-diagnosis.headline: fNIRS autism classifiers fall to near chance when the time window shifts
autism-diagnosis.summary: fNIRS autism classifiers assume aligned time windows, yet hemodynamic delay differs between people. A benchmark varied windows from 2.5 to 10 s and tested three vision models and eight adaptation strategies, leave-one-subject-out, N=124. Zero-shot accuracy dropped to 54–69%; fine-tuning on about 5% subject data recovered 90–96%, and domain-adversarial or self-supervised methods reached 78–90%.

summaryParts.problem: fNIRS autism classifiers assume aligned time windows, yet hemodynamic delay differs between people.
summaryParts.approach: A benchmark varied windows from 2.5 to 10 s and tested three vision models and eight adaptation strategies, leave-one-subject-out, N=124.
summaryParts.result: Zero-shot accuracy dropped to 54–69%; fine-tuning on about 5% subject data recovered 90–96%, and domain-adversarial or self-supervised methods reached 78–90%.
summaryParts.limits: One biological-motion task; the abstract reports cross-validation only.

autism-diagnosis.originalTitle: Frozen Brain-MRI Foundation Models Are Site Fingerprints
autism-diagnosis.catchyTitle: Frozen Brain-MRI Foundation Models Are Site Fingerprints
autism-diagnosis.headline: Brain-MRI foundation-model embeddings encode scanner site more strongly than autism diagnosis
autism-diagnosis.summary: Frozen MRI foundation-model embeddings are widely assumed to capture anatomy. Audit of three frozen 3-D encoders at every depth on the ABIDE-I and ABIDE-II autism cohorts. Site was linearly decodable at about 0.9 balanced accuracy, above sex, age or diagnosis, even with random weights; null-space projection or ComBat cut it to 0.07 or 0.00.

summaryParts.problem: Frozen MRI foundation-model embeddings are widely assumed to capture anatomy.
summaryParts.approach: Audit of three frozen 3-D encoders at every depth on the ABIDE-I and ABIDE-II autism cohorts.
summaryParts.result: Site was linearly decodable at about 0.9 balanced accuracy, above sex, age or diagnosis, even with random weights; null-space projection or ComBat cut it to 0.07 or 0.00.
summaryParts.limits: Removing site signal harms segmentation, because site and anatomy are entangled.

ai-mental-health.originalTitle: PatientAct: Theory-Grounded Mental Health Client Simulation
ai-mental-health.catchyTitle: PatientAct: Theory-Grounded Mental Health Client Simulation
ai-mental-health.headline: Theory-grounded client simulator beats baselines on resistance realism
ai-mental-health.summary: LLM-simulated counseling clients are too cooperative: they disclose readily and resolve core issues in one session. Profiles follow the 5Ps case formulation; memories unlock at trust thresholds, and emotion is modeled before each reply. Across 40 clinical situations, profiles were diverse and clinically plausible, outperforming baselines on resistance quality and behavioral realism.

ai-mental-health.headline: On LLM personas, text features explain up to 76% of anxiety variance
ai-mental-health.summary: NLP models that predict mental-health outcomes rarely state what signal they measure. Nine persona-conditioned LLMs completed questionnaires; emotion and network features fed random forests, explained with SHAP. Models explained up to 76.0% of DASS-21 anxiety variance in personas and separated clinical from control human transcripts with up to 68% accuracy.

blockchain.originalTitle: 0xPass: A Secure Protocol for Universal Cross-Chain Accounts
blockchain.catchyTitle: 0xPass: A Secure Protocol for Universal Cross-Chain Accounts
blockchain.headline: 0xPass layers cross-chain accounts so no node holds a full signing key
blockchain.summary: Universal cross-chain accounts create trust problems in authentication, key custody, signing and recovery. A modular protocol separates request orchestration, transaction solving and signing, using threshold signatures and constrained delegation. It sets out a staged path from a centrally run service to a permissionless network with rotating key-management committees.

summaryParts.problem: Universal cross-chain accounts create trust problems in authentication, key custody, signing and recovery.
summaryParts.approach: A modular protocol separates request orchestration, transaction solving and signing, using threshold signatures and constrained delegation.
summaryParts.result: It sets out a staged path from a centrally run service to a permissionless network with rotating key-management committees.
summaryParts.limits: Design paper; the abstract reports no formal proof or benchmarks.

recall.question: What prevents any single 0xPass node from signing alone?
recall.answer: Threshold signatures split the signing key across nodes.

surveillance-anomaly-detection.headline: 10th AI City Challenge draws 325 teams across six perception tracks
surveillance-anomaly-detection.summary: Smart-city perception needs shared benchmarks for multi-camera tracking, anomaly reasoning and forecasting. The ECCV 2026 edition ran six tracks, including multi-camera 3D perception, traffic anomaly reasoning and text-based person anomaly search. 325 teams from 26 countries and regions took part, up from 245 and 15; strong entries combined foundation models with geometric grounding and synthetic data.

summaryParts.approach: The ECCV 2026 edition ran six tracks, including multi-camera 3D perception, traffic anomaly reasoning and text-based person anomaly search.
summaryParts.result: 325 teams from 26 countries and regions took part, up from 245 and 15; strong entries combined foundation models with geometric grounding and synthetic data.
summaryParts.limits: Workshop summary of leaderboards, not a new method.

recall.question: Name two of the six primary tracks in the 2026 AI City Challenge.
recall.answer: Any two of: multi-camera 3D perception, safety captioning/VQA, traffic anomaly reasoning, text-based person anomaly search, generative traffic forecasting, cross-city detection.

matrixRow.result: 325 teams; foundation models + geometric grounding win

surveillance-anomaly-detection.originalTitle: RISE: Roadside Infrastructure Sequence Understanding across 3D Tracking and Structured Vision-Language Reasoning
surveillance-anomaly-detection.catchyTitle: RISE: Roadside Infrastructure Sequence Understanding across 3D Tracking and Structured Vision-Language Reasoning
surveillance-anomaly-detection.headline: LiDAR-free 3D tracking across roadside cameras, with a 33,910-question benchmark
surveillance-anomaly-detection.summary: Roadside multi-camera systems need persistent 3D tracks and reasoning about what happens next. SAM3 video identities are matched across calibrated views; an MLLM pipeline builds box-grounded predictive questions. Tracks reach 66.9 MOTA on 20 reviewed clips from six intersections; RISE-VQA holds 33,910 QA pairs from 557 clips.

summaryParts.problem: Roadside multi-camera systems need persistent 3D tracks and reasoning about what happens next.
summaryParts.approach: SAM3 video identities are matched across calibrated views; an MLLM pipeline builds box-grounded predictive questions.
summaryParts.result: Tracks reach 66.9 MOTA on 20 reviewed clips from six intersections; RISE-VQA holds 33,910 QA pairs from 557 clips.
summaryParts.limits: Models still struggle with spatial grounding and future localization.
